national.line: A high school teacher in Sandy Springs, Georgia, found a tiny black cat stuck in her car engine on the way to work, and it turned into a surprise gift right before her Halloween wedding anniversary.
The 2026 Dog Photography Awards named 18 finalists, and a photographer named Caldwell took home a trophy for a photo championing bully breeds like the pit bull.
Tom Petty was born 76 years ago today in Gainesville, Florida, and as an 11-year-old he met Elvis Presley, the moment that sparked his love of rock and roll.
A sixth grader's science experiment set out to answer a question nobody knew they needed answered: whether a cat's backside really touches every surface it sits on.
Couples therapists say the simple move that cools down almost any argument is one person being willing to go first, because most fights do not actually need a winner.
A dog in New Hampshire went viral zooming through big piles of leaves as the fall colors there hit their peak.
Walmart is rolling out a new membership bundle that combines Walmart Plus and Sam's Club Plus into one package.
Rescuers in Florida pulled a dog out of a sinkhole, and the pup made it out safe.

pride.label: National Award
pride.line: Lebanon R-3 Schools has earned a National Meritorious Budget Award.

pride.label: New Coach
pride.line: Brittany Stamm has been named the new head girls basketball coach for Lebanon R-3 Schools.

pride.label: New Coach
pride.line: Kalem Copling has been named the new head boys basketball coach for Lebanon R-3 Schools.

pride.label: Grand Opening
pride.line: Lebanon R-3 Schools celebrated the opening of its new Robert W. Plaster Center for Student Success.

pride.label: Band Honors
pride.line: The Lebanon Jackets placed at the Valhalla Marching Festival.

pride.label: World Food Champs
pride.line: Molly McDermitt, Cycila Keeney and Samantha Etheridge, culinary arts students from the Waynesville Career Center under Chef Jon Dye, competed in the finals of the World Food Championships in Indianapolis on Oct. 18 with a dish called Bacon Lover's Christmas.

pride.label: Student of the Month
pride.line: Christina Smithey, a senior at Waynesville High School, was named the Rotary Student of the Month for October, recognized at the Oct. 13 Rotary Club of Pulaski County meeting for her blood drives and community service.

pride.label: District Band
pride.line: Payton Rushing, Ericah Njuguna, Tyler Silbanuz, Ethan Schnacke, Vivien Lu, Zoe Striplin, Alexzander Romans, Myra Archer Gutierrez, Aliyah Bowers, Kevin Connor, Aiden York, Jenna Ballard, Juliet Piper, Matthew Hinton, Mikaila Knight, Haley Brown, Landon Boswell, Harley Atchison and Zayden Fikes, from Waynesville High School, made the Central District Band after auditions at Rolla High School on Oct. 13.

pride.label: Band Award
pride.line: The Waynesville High School Tiger Pride Marching Band took third place overall and the Outstanding Winds Award for the highest music score at the Valhalla Marching Band Festival in Springfield on Oct. 3.

pride.label: Teacher Shout-Out
pride.line: Michael McGuire, a teacher at Wood Elementary, got this week's Teacher Proud Tuesday shout-out from the Waynesville R-6 School District.

pride.label: 100 Years in Business
pride.line: Marshfield Chevrolet is celebrating 100 years of serving the Marshfield community.

pride.label: New Leader
pride.line: Keith Klostermann, a 30-year educator, has been appointed the new city administrator for Osage Beach.

pride.label: State Honor
pride.line: Buffalo Alderman Eric Kirchberg has earned the designation of Certified Municipal Official from the Missouri Municipal League's Municipal Governance Institute.

local.line: The Hive Depot is providing essential resources and learning opportunities for students in Lebanon R-3 Schools.
A Lebanon church built a ramp for a disabled woman so she can get in and out of her home more easily.
Another new logo has been proposed for the City of Lebanon.
Members of the Waynesville High School Class of 1966 toured today's high school during their reunion and donated 775 dollars to the district's Snack in a Pack program for students in need.
The Waynesville R-6 School District is marking National School Bus Safety Week through Oct. 23 and thanking its transportation team for keeping students safe every day.
Residents of Colonial Springs Healthcare Center in Buffalo traveled to Bolivar on Oct. 9 to compete in the Golden Age Games.
A group called Shine Through Faith is bringing helping hands to Marshfield, mowing yards, picking up groceries and checking on elderly neighbors.
A new 126-room Hyatt hotel is planned in Backwater Jacks' Cove at Lake of the Ozarks.
A Lake of the Ozarks nonprofit is helping women start over by offering hope, housing and support.
Patrick Mahomes does not have a home at Lake of the Ozarks, despite the rumors, and his mom says so herself.
Lake of the Ozarks hit a new heat record last Tuesday.
The Dallas County Library has new books on the shelf, including The Mountains We Call Home by Kim Michele Richardson.

music.line: The CMA is giving its Dolly Parton tribute its own TV special instead of a short segment on the 2026 CMA Awards in November.
Blake Shelton made a surprise appearance at the Country Music Hall of Fame ceremony and got big laughs telling how his Paul Overstreet song turned out to be 'Some Beach.'
Zach Top is expanding his Cold Beer and Country Music Tour with more shows.
On this day in 2023, Luke Combs hit number one with a cover song that helped a folk legend make country music history.
Carly Pearce has released the music video for her song 'Same Circus.'
Brothers Osborne have a new album called 'Watertown' on the way.

weird.line: An angler at Lake of the Ozarks set a new world record by reeling in a 164-pound paddlefish.
Sixty years ago this month, a Buffalo woman named Mrs. Jimmie Hayes found a two-headed lizard on her porch and put it on display, according to the Buffalo Reflex.
Biologists netted a 70-pound lake sturgeon below a Missouri River dam and found a tag the size of a grain of rice showing the fish had swum 681 miles upstream in nine years.
An Asian elephant named Samudra squished a 500-pound pumpkin flat during the Oregon Zoo's 28th annual Squishing of the Squash.
A grower has produced the first pumpkin ever to break the 3,000-pound barrier.
A 61-year-old grandmother of 12 broke her own world record by holding a plank for five hours.
A rare blue-tinted alligator was rescued and taken in at Gatorland in Florida.
A black bear was caught on camera boxing a punching bag on a Southern California patio like a seasoned pro.
A bear was caught on camera opening a fridge and walking off with an alcoholic drink in Golden Gate Estates, Florida.
An emu that ran away from its owner tried its best to outrun police officers before it was finally rounded up.
Emergency crews in Monroe, New Jersey, helped a herd of escaped goats find their way back home.
Veronica the runaway cow is back home after rescuers pulled her out of deep mud.
A mare in Ohio has set the world record for the longest horse tail.
A mysterious white shape on the Alaska tundra turned out to be an albino caribou that had not been seen for decades.
A scorched, foreign-looking object found in a Minnesota crop field has people trying to figure out what it is.
A traveler was baffled when an airport self-checkout machine asked him to leave an 18 percent tip, and his question was simple: who am I tipping here?
Matthew Inman of The Oatmeal built a giant, evil Halloween version of Jimothy, the viral short and round Seattle raccoon, in his brother's front yard on Bainbridge Island.
A tiny dog played the drums in a rock band costume at the 36th annual Tompkins Square Halloween Dog Parade.
In South Carolina, children wrote goodbye letters for a senior shelter dog, the letters went viral, and the dog got adopted.
A small bear was spotted wandering through a neighborhood in San Luis Obispo County, California.
A moose was spotted on the loose in Brewster.
Scientists have discovered a bizarre squid-like creature from the Jurassic period unlike anything ever seen before.
